correctness.rationale: For all d>=1 the 2d-point DFT on each circle kills the intensity-difference coefficients at all orders |k|<d. The only aliased mode has coefficient R^d(a_d conjugate(a_0)-b_d conjugate(b_0)); the two real projections are invertible if and only if sin(d(psi-phi)) is nonzero. Continuous modulus equality on distinct radii makes the rational quotient invariant under a positive dilation, hence constant by its Laurent expansion. Explicit z versus radius and 1 plus/minus i exp(-id phi) z^d witnesses prove both failures. Direct verification of the subsystems and finite checker (5784 checks for degrees 1 through 8) corroborates but does not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: Distinct from the published finite-dimensional phase-retrieval constructions: Pohl–Li–Boche uses 2d+1 and 2d-1 samples, Bodmann–Hammen uses intersecting circles, and Chalendar–Partington proves continuous-circle uniqueness rather than this discrete balanced-polygon alias condition. Earlier quadratic and cubic cases are subsumed, but not conversely. Current source and semantic-index searches did not find a covering all-degree theorem. Historical priority remains a bounded, non-independent assessment.
residual_risks: Historical priority is not independently certified: an unindexed equivalent statement or a stronger uninspected theorem could cover this precise allocation.

The classification combines elementary finite Fourier interpolation with previously established continuous two-circle rigidity; its originality is the all-degree balanced grid criterion and necessity witnesses, not either classical ingredient in isolation.

value.rationale: A complete necessary-and-sufficient criterion for every balanced two-regular-polygon arrangement is a motivated classification of structured Fourier-phase measurements. It includes all complex polynomials of arbitrarily high degree, two explicit sharp obstruction mechanisms, direct Fourier coefficient demixing and the optimal angular phase offset for that normalized linear subsystem. These conclusions are not merely a fixed-degree numeric variant; no global minimal measurement count or nonlinear noise stability is asserted.
